talks.title: Blind Trailer Shouting
talks.summary: Tanker trailers have a powerline network, PLC4TRUCKS, which is unintentionally accessible wirelessly (CVEs 2020-14514 and 2022-26131). Newer trailer brake controllers use diagnostic protocol KWP2000, secured with access control by seed-key. The talk shows Wireshark analysis of that diagnostic traffic and two ways past the access control: an SMT solver on a few request-response pairs, and a reset attack that makes seeds predictable. The second way is a blind wireless attack, CVE-2024-12054. The brake controller is also exposed to trailer-installed telematics. The work comes from onsite and bench tests of heavy vehicles.

talks.title: Direct Memory, Access Everywhere
talks.summary: DMA vulnerabilities are not new, and most systems are still open to them because the attacks are treated as difficult and testing is weak. Epic Erebus is a small portable tool for those attacks. It is an open PCIe implementation with control over Transaction Layer Packets, so the bus and the DMA mitigations can be inspected. The talk covers what Erebus can do, how to use it, and what to check when DMA mitigations are configured.

talks.title: Ghosts of REvil: An Inside Look with the Hacker Behind the Kaseya Ransomware Attack
talks.summary: Yaroslav Vasinskyi was sentenced in 2024 to 13 years in U.S. federal prison for his role in the Kaseya ransomware attack. Threat researcher Jon DiMaggio spoke with him by phone and email over the following year. John Fokker, formerly a Dutch cybercrime investigator on operations against REvil, joins the talk. They describe how REvil operated, what happened in the Kaseya attack, and how the crew came apart. The speakers page also says the session includes new information on leadership that remains at large.

talks.title: Advanced Active Directory to Entra ID lateral movement techniques
talks.summary: The talk asks whether a hybrid environment still has a security boundary between Active Directory and Entra ID. Hardening has reduced how far the cloud trusts on-premises data, because threat actors have used known lateral-movement paths into the cloud. It walks through Entra ID and hybrid trust internals and several lateral-movement techniques that start from on-premises AD, including paths that bypass authentication and MFA. The speakers page describes them as design behavior rather than vulnerabilities, with some later hardening from Microsoft and little useful logging.

talks.title: Claude--Climbing a CTF Scoreboard Near You
talks.summary: The talk follows Claude through cybersecurity competitions: defending networks at CCDC and working PicoCTF and HackTheBox challenges. The speakers page cites a top-3% PicoCTF placement and red-team defense at CCDC, and also failures such as drifting into security philosophy and inventing flags. It covers tooling harnesses and keeping the assistant coherent across long competitions.

talks.title: ChromeAlone: Transforming a Browser into a C2 Platform
talks.summary: The talk shows how legacy and newer Chrome features can be used to mimic a conventional command-and-control implant while avoiding traditional endpoint protection. ChromeAlone proxies raw TCP, phishes for YubiKey codes, dumps cookies and credentials, keylogs browser windows, and runs shell commands. It sideloads components without user interaction and obfuscates code with WebAssembly.

talks.title: Patching Critical Infrastructure: Announcing the Winners of DARPA's AI Cyber Challenge
talks.summary: DARPA and ARPA-H ran the AI Cyber Challenge, a two-year competition to build systems that find and fix software vulnerabilities. This talk announces the winners, covers the challenges and lessons, and discusses what it would take to deploy the tools, which were to be open sourced after DEF CON. The speakers page lists first, second, and third prizes of $4 million, $3 million, and $1.5 million. The media-server file also names Jason Roos, who is not a speaker on the speakers page; the page lists Jim O'Neill instead.
